methodological_rigor.justification: Ex vivo patient meningioma treatment with 8803 (STING agonist), preclinical models (orthotopic immunocompetent), integrated molecular profiling (ATAC-seq, RNA-seq, flow). Mechanistic validation through gasdermin D induction, necroptosis pathway characterization. However: no sample size justification for patient ex vivo studies, limited patient specimens, murine models may not recapitulate human disease complexity.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Demonstrates STING agonist (8803) inducible activity in meningioma, a CNS tumor lacking established systemic therapies. Mechanism validated: gasdermin D-mediated necroptosis, immune infiltration, TME remodeling. However, clinical translation requires human validation; necroptosis as primary anti-tumor mechanism less established than apoptosis/cell lysis.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe mouse models, patient sample preparation, molecular assays (ATAC-seq, RNA-seq, flow cytometry). Missing: ARRIVE checklist adherence statement, sample size justification, formal statistical approaches, data availability statements for sequencing/flow data.

novelty_literature.justification: Demonstrates STING agonist efficacy in meningioma context with mechanistic validation. STING pathway and gasdermin D-mediated necroptosis individually well-characterized. Application to meningioma population with genomic basis (STING hypomethylation) and functional validation is novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Methods and results logically organized. Some redundancy between abstract findings and text. Figures effectively integrate ex vivo patient work with in vivo preclinical validation and molecular profiling.

key_strengths: Demonstration of STING agonist (8803) activity in diverse patient meningiomas ex vivo with mechanistic validation via gasdermin D induction
Integrated molecular profiling linking genomic features (STING locus hypomethylation, chromatin accessibility) to pharmacologic responsiveness
In vivo efficacy in orthotopic immunocompetent meningioma model with immune infiltration and TME remodeling
Mechanistic pathway elucidation: direct tumor necroptosis triggering macrophage activation and ECM degradation
key_concerns: Limited patient sample size for ex vivo studies; no prospective sample size calculation or power analysis provided
Mechanistic novelty limited: STING activation and gasdermin D-mediated necroptosis individually established; integration to meningioma is contextual
No formal statistical framework or correction for multiple testing across molecular assays
Clinical translation unvalidated in patients; necroptosis pathway less established as primary mechanism than apoptosis
Data availability statements absent for sequencing and flow cytometry raw data
chief_reviewer.rationale: Mechanistically sound preclinical work with integrated patient data. Preclinical stage limits tier placement despite novel disease application.
